tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session logs show a complete, deterministic sequence that creates a subcategory under an existing category: navigate to the categories page, dismiss an incoming admin notice, select a parent tree node, click Add Subcategory, fill the form fields (Name, URL Key, Is Active, Include in Menu, Description, Page Title, Meta Description) and Save. Recorded element hashes and common Magento id attributes (name, url_key, meta_title, meta_description, description, save) were captured and used to build stable selectors.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose tool: create a new subcategory under a provided parent category and set the most commonly used category attributes. It assumes the automation context (browser session) is already authenticated in Magento admin and the user executing the tool has the necessary permissions.

Action Plan (detailed):
1) Navigate to the admin categories URL.
2) Wait briefly for JS and potential loading mask.
3) Close the incoming admin notice if present.
4) Select the parent category in the left-hand tree by visible text prefix.
5) Click 'Add Subcategory' and wait for the New Subcategory form to load.
6) Fill required and optional fields: name (required), url_key, is_active (Yes/No), include_in_menu (Yes/No), description (textarea), page_title, meta_description.
7) Click Save Category and wait for the server round-trip to complete.
8) Extract page content for a final verification step.

Variable Identification (inputs required):
- admin_categories_url: specific admin categories URL used for navigation (recorded value used as default). Optional override.
- parent_category_name: visible parent category text (prefix match) — required.
- name: category Name — required by Magento.
- url_key: URL key/slug — optional.
- is_active: visible text option 'Yes' or 'No' — optional; use visible text because the demo UI presents a select.
- include_in_menu: visible text option 'Yes' or 'No' — optional.
- description: free text for the description textarea — optional.
- page_title: meta_title — optional.
- meta_description: meta description textarea — optional.

Step Optimization and Justification:
- Navigation to the categories page uses the recorded URL to avoid intermediate clicks. (PASS 2 optimization: direct URL navigation is deterministic and faster.)
- Dismissal of the Incoming Message notice is included because it blocked interactions in the recorded run; selector uses a text/title-based XPath with the recorded elementHash as a backup.
- Parent category selection uses an XPath that matches the visible label start (starts-with) to avoid brittle exact-match against dynamic counts in parentheses.
- Add Subcategory click matches either <button> or <a> renderings using a union XPath and selects the first match to be robust across admin theme variants.
- Form fields target stable id/name attributes (#name, #url_key, textarea#description, #meta_title, #meta_description). For boolean controls the tool uses visible option text (Yes/No) since the demo UI uses selects for these fields.
- Save uses id '#save' when available and falls back to button title/text XPath; the recorded elementHash is included to assist in locating the same control if needed.

Deterministic behavior:
- All steps are sequential and deterministic; no branching. The tool is single-purpose (create subcategory). It uses explicit waits where the recorded session required them and targets stable attributes/text. The tool avoids reliance on CSS class-only selectors and uses id/name or label/text-based XPaths where appropriate.

Limitations and caveats:
- This tool assumes the browser session is already authenticated; no login flow is included.
- WYSIWYG behaviour: when tinyMCE or similar editors are active the visible editor may be an iframe; this tool writes into the underlying textarea. If your environment requires editing the iframe body directly, add a step to switch context into the iframe and set the iframe body text.
- If the admin theme of the target environment is heavily customized (different id/name values) selectors may need adjustment. The tool includes the most common Magento 1.x admin attribute names to maximize compatibility.

Essentiality:
- The tool includes only steps required to create a subcategory and set attributes; it does not perform extraneous filtering, sorting, or unrelated navigation.
name: magento_create_subcategory
description: Create a subcategory under an existing Magento admin category and set common category attributes (name, url_key, is_active, include_in_menu, description, page_title, meta_description). Navigates to the Magento Admin Categories page, selects the parent category, clicks Add Subcategory, fills fields, and saves. Assumes the automation context is already authenticated in the Magento admin (no login step).

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Admin Categories page. If admin_categories_url is empty the recorded default URL 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_category/' will be used.
Allow page JS to initialize and any loading masks to appear; short static wait before interacting.
Dismiss the 'Incoming Message' / admin notice if present. Selector matches the close link; elementHash is recorded as a stable backup.
Short wait after closing a notice so the page layout stabilizes.
Select the parent category in the left-hand category tree. The XPath uses starts-with to ignore dynamic counts in parentheses (e.g., 'Default Category (1893)').
Wait for the category edit form to load after selecting the tree node (AJAX).
Click the 'Add Subcategory' control in the Categories toolbar. Matches either <button> or <a> renderings and selects the first match.
Wait for the New Subcategory form to appear and any WYSIWYG initialization to start.
Set the Name field for the new subcategory. Uses id 'name' or name='name' depending on the admin markup.
Set the URL Key if a value was provided. If {url_key} is empty the field will be set to an empty string (caller should pass value only when update is desired).

Set the 'Is Active' control by visible option text (use 'Yes' or 'No'). If {is_active} is not provided this step will attempt to select an empty value and thus should be supplied when a change is desired.
Set the 'Include in Navigation Menu' option by visible text ('Yes' or 'No'). If omitted caller should leave blank to avoid changes.
Set the category description into the underlying textarea. If the WYSIWYG editor is active it usually mirrors this textarea; automation environments should ensure the editor has synced the value.
Set the Page Title / meta_title field if provided.
Set the Meta Description textarea if provided.
Short wait to ensure form values are registered before save.
Click the Save Category action. Uses id '#save' when present, falls back to the button text/title XPath; elementHash recorded from the demonstration is included as a backup.
Wait for the save action to complete (server round-trip). You may increase this wait when automating slow test environments.
Capture the page to allow the caller to verify success (for example look for 'was successfully saved' messages or the new category name in the page header).
steps.goal: Confirm success message or extract the current category header to verify the new subcategory was created/loaded

input_schema.name: admin_categories_url
input_schema.description: Full URL to the Magento Admin Categories page. Example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_category/'. If omitted the tool will navigate to the recorded URL.

input_schema.name: parent_category_name
input_schema.description: Visible text prefix of the parent category shown in the left tree (exact visible name or the start of it). Example: 'Default Category' or 'Men'. Use the visible name (omit dynamic counts in parentheses).

input_schema.name: url_key
input_schema.description: Category URL Key (slug). Example: 'bot-subcategory-demo-2026'. If omitted the url_key field is not modified.

input_schema.name: is_active
input_schema.description: Visible option for the 'Is Active' control. Use the visible text ('Yes' or 'No'). If omitted the control is not changed.

input_schema.name: include_in_menu
input_schema.description: Visible option for the 'Include in Navigation Menu' control. Use visible text ('Yes' or 'No'). If omitted the control is not changed.

input_schema.name: description
input_schema.description: Category description (plain text). If WYSIWYG is enabled the underlying textarea is targeted; the tool attempts to set the textarea value.

input_schema.name: page_title
input_schema.description: Meta page title (meta_title). If omitted the field is not changed.

input_schema.name: meta_description
input_schema.description: Meta description for the category. If omitted the field is not changed.
